title: Operational Continuity Blueprint for Responder Teams
author: Elena Morales
content:
SUMMARY
This blueprint codifies the continuity patterns and responder workflows used by Redwood teams to detect, triage, mitigate, and learn from service incidents. It is intended for engineers, platform SREs, and customer-facing stakeholders who participate in on-call rotations, game days, and post-incident analysis.

SCOPE
- Services: applies to Redwood API, Serving Runtime (gpu-runner), Model Router, KV Cache, and Console backends.
- Incident classes: latency/throughput SLO regressions, partial service degradations, region failovers, configuration regressions, and data integrity issues.
- Out of scope: purely product design bugs without production impact; internal docs/drive outages.

KEY OBJECTIVES
1) Maintain customer-visible continuity: preserve 99.9% availability for Redwood API across hosted regions during single-region faults.
2) Reduce mean time to restore (MTTR) through standardized runbooks and automated containment.
3) Capture learning via a lightweight post-incident process and measurable action items.

TERMS & DEFINITIONS
- Primary responder: on-call engineer assigned to initial triage.
- Incident commander (IC): person coordinating cross-team response for SEV >= 2.
- Escalation window: 15 minutes from pager trigger for SEV 1; 30 minutes for SEV 2.
- Severity definitions: SEV 1 (full outage), SEV 2 (major degradation), SEV 3 (partial impact / reduced capacity).

OWNERSHIP AND ROSTER
- Primary ownership: Platform SREs for infra-level issues, Serving Runtime for model-serving faults, Eng Developer Experience for API-level regressions.
- Contact matrix: see table below for primary and secondary contacts.

| Service Area | Primary Team | Primary Responder | Secondary/Backup |
|--------------|--------------|-------------------|------------------|
| Redwood API (public) | Eng DevEx | api-oncall | platform-oncall |
| Serving Runtime (gpu-runner) | Eng Serving Runtime | runtime-oncall | infra-oncall |
| Model Router | Eng Platform | router-oncall | runtime-oncall |
| KV Cache | Eng Infra | cache-oncall | runtime-oncall |
| Console / Observability | Eng Platform | console-oncall | api-oncall |

SLOS AND ALERT THRESHOLDS
- Redwood API availability: 99.9% monthly target. Alert: 5% drop in success rate over 5m -> SEV2.
- P50 latency target (completion): 150ms for embeddings; alert at sustained 3x baseline over 10m -> SEV2.
- Token generation tail latency (p99): target 500ms on hosted small models; alert at p99 > 2s -> SEV2.
- Throughput saturation: queue length > 3000 requests for 2m -> SEV1 if API errors increase >2%.

INCIDENT LIFECYCLE - PROCEDURE
1) Detect & Classify
   a) Pager or internal alert triggers; any engineer can declare an incident in the incident channel.
   b) Confirm signal: check primary dashboards (availability, error budget, RPC error rates) and distributed traces.
   c) Assign severity using thresholds above.
2) Mobilize & Contain
   a) Primary responder acknowledges within escalation window.
   b) IC assigned for SEV1/SEV2 within 10 minutes.
   c) Rapid containment: apply traffic redirection, autoscale reserved pools, enable model-variant fallback, or throttle non-essential routes.
3) Diagnose & Mitigate
   a) Run targeted runbooks (examples below).
   b) Capture timeline notes in the incident doc and update status page draft.
   c) Implement a mitigation (hotfix, config rollback, capacity increase).
4) Restore & Validate
   a) Confirm SLOs have returned to normal for a sustained window (15m for SEV2, 60m for SEV1).
   b) Remove emergency mitigations and observe.
5) Close & Learn
   a) Open a post-incident report within 48 hours (lightweight) and complete full postmortem within 7 business days for SEV1/SEV2.
   b) Track action items with owners and target dates.

RUNBOOK EXAMPLES (copyable steps)
- Scenario: API 5xx spike for hosted text-generation\ 1) Check API gateway metrics: 5xx rate, origin downstream latency, rate of rejected requests.\ 2) Confirm whether errors are internal model timeouts or rate-limiter rejections.\ 3) If model timeouts: switch traffic to a lower-cost model variant via Model Router (command below).
   Example command: curl -X POST https://internal-router.local/route/switch -d '{service: "text-gen", variant: "v1-small"}'
 4) Enable autoscale burst for Dedicated pools for 15 minutes: kubectl scale --replicas=10 deployment/dedicated-gpu-pool
 5) Open a short customer notice draft (template below) and post preliminary message to status.redwood.ai

- Scenario: KV cache corruption detected (inconsistent embeddings)\ 1) Quarantine affected cache cluster (remove write traffic).\ 2) Switch reads to recent snapshot store and enable read-through from primary DB.\ 3) Run integrity scanner: python tools/cache_integrity_check.py --cluster=cluster-a --since=2026-02-01\ 4) If snapshot restore required, follow restore checklist and notify CS for customer impact assessment.

COMMUNICATIONS - TEMPLATES
- Status page short:
  Title: Degraded API performance in us-west-2\  Impact: Some customers may see increased error rates and higher tail latency for text generation.\  Current status: Mitigation in progress; traffic partially routed to alternative region.\  Next update: in 20 minutes or when situation changes.

- Customer-facing e-mail template (use for SEV1/SEV2):
  Subject: Incident update: Redwood API performance degradation (Incident ID: {{INCIDENT_ID}})

  Hello {{Customer Name}},

  We are investigating an issue affecting Redwood API performance that may impact requests to text generation and embeddings. Our engineers have applied traffic routing mitigations and are actively restoring service. We will provide another update by {{NEXT_UPDATE_TIME}}.

  What we know: increased 5xx rate for requests routed to us-west-2 between {{START_TIME}} and now.
  What we are doing: routing traffic to alternate regions and enabling fallback model variants to reduce error rates.
  Who to contact: your Customer Success Manager at {{CSM_EMAIL}} for account-specific questions.

  Status updates: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/{{INCIDENT_ID}}

  Thank you for your patience,
  Redwood Support Team

POST-INCIDENT TEMPLATE (for SEV1/SEV2)
- Title: Short descriptive headline
- Incident ID: {{INCIDENT_ID}}
- Severity: SEV1/SEV2/SEV3
- Timeline: ordered list with UTC timestamps
- Root cause hypothesis and analysis: concise summary
- Corrective actions taken during incident: list with timestamps
- Long-term remediation items: owner and due date for each
- Metrics impacted and regression windows: graphs or links to dashboards
- Customer impact summary: affected customers and mitigation status
- Final status and verification steps

ON-CALL ROTATION POLICY (high-level)
- Cadence: weekly primary rotations for primary responders, fortnightly for IC pool.
- Handover: outgoing on-call must run the Handover Checklist in the on-call channel including known escalations, ongoing mitigations, and open action items.
- Backup coverage: secondary must be reachable by phone/sms and acknowledged within 30 minutes for SEV1.
- Vacation/absence: delegate via the on-call schedule tool and notify the rotation owner 72 hours in advance.

SAMPLE ROTATION SCHEDULE (quarter view)
| Week Start | Primary | Secondary | IC Pool |
|------------|---------|-----------|---------|
| 2026-03-01 | Maya L. | runtime-oncall | IC-Group-A |
| 2026-03-08 | Carlos V. | api-oncall | IC-Group-B |
| 2026-03-15 | Arun P. | infra-oncall | IC-Group-A |

GAME DAY FRAMEWORK
- Objective: validate recovery patterns and measure MTTR for targeted failure modes.
- Duration: half-day (4 hours) or full-day (8 hours) depending on scope.
- Roles: facilitator, observers (metrics & tracing), primary responder, IC, customer comms lead.
- Measured outcomes: time to detect, time to assign IC, time to mitigate, time to restore, quality of status updates.
- Example scenarios: region outage, model-variant regression with degraded quality, cache cluster partial partition.
- Post-game checklist: update runbooks, add automated detection where manual steps took >5 minutes, schedule follow-up action owners.

AFTER-ACTION & METRICS
- Track MTTA (mean time to acknowledge), MTTR, percentage of runbook steps automated, and number of customer minutes impacted.
- Quarterly review: incidents and game-day results presented at SRE forum with a 3-item improvement plan.

DOCUMENT LINKS & REFERENCES
- Related runbook index: /confluence/runbook-index (link placeholder)
- Escalation matrix and contact directory: /confluence/escalation-directory
- Observable dashboards: grafana.redwood.ai/d/incident-overview

APPENDIX: QUICK CHECKLISTS (copyable)
- Immediate triage checklist (first 10 minutes):
  1) Acknowledge pager and set channel to incident-{{INCIDENT_ID}}
  2) Check global health dashboard and API gateway error rates
  3) Identify whether mitigation is routing, scaling, or rollback
  4) Draft status page note and set next update cadence

- Handover checklist (end of shift):
  1) Confirm mitigations are removed or handed to owner
  2) Update incident doc with current state and next steps
  3) Transfer on-call in schedule tool and ping new primary in channel

END OF DOCUMENT

If you have questions or suggested edits, ping the author on slack @elena.m or raise a documentation change request in the docs repo.
